name: ClickUp
summary: The 'everything app' for project and work management. Centralize your tasks, docs, sprints, and team communication in one hub.
best_for: teams that want one highly customizable app for tasks, docs, goals and reporting and will invest in setting it up
skip_if: you want something simple your team adopts in a day — ClickUp's depth becomes overwhelm for a light use case
honest_knock: The everything-app breadth is also the downside — it's feature-dense with a real learning curve, and teams can drown in options. Powerful and cheap per seat, but only if you'll actually configure and adopt it.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 23 October 2026 on the Free Forever plan with one seat and no payment method: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We imported a CSV file with three made-up tasks (each with a status, a start date, a due date and a description), compared what arrived with the file, and exported the whole workspace.
findings: The spreadsheet importer (Settings > Imports / Exports) matched all five columns of our CSV to ClickUp fields automatically, then mapped the three status values one to one and previewed 3 valid rows before 'Import into ClickUp'. The three tasks landed in a new list, each under its own status, and the task we opened had the right status, both dates and its description.

The import history said 'Imported 23 items' for our file of three rows, while the new list held exactly the three tasks. The counter and the result did not agree; we did not find out what the 23 counts.

The workspace export downloaded within seconds as a CSV of 15 rows (the 12 sample tasks plus our 3) with 34 columns, including task ID, link, content, status, dates, subtasks, attachments, assignees, tags, priority, location, time tracking, checklists and comments. All three of our tasks came back with status, description and both dates.
Dates in the export appear as epoch values and as text with a time zone, set to 04:00 although our file held only dates.

Onboarding took seven screens, with an extra confirmation to skip inviting people ('Skip without inviting'). Billing showed 'Free Forever, 1 seat · $0 / seat' and 'No payment methods', and the workspace came with three sample lists holding 12 tasks.

The upload window inside ClickUp did not respond to our browser tool, so we loaded the file in the same import session through a separate tab; that is a quirk of our test setup, not something we can pin on ClickUp.
not_tested: Exporting views (List, Table, Form) and the Free Forever limit of five
Automations, ClickUp Brain and multiple users
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.

vendor_mcp.what: Hosted server at mcp.clickup.com/mcp covering tasks, docs, time tracking, workspace search and chat. Delete operations are deliberately not supported.
vendor_mcp.plan: All plans. Free: 50 calls a day; Unlimited and above: 300 a day on a rolling 24-hour window; with the Everything AI add-on you get the standard public API limits.
vendor_mcp.note: The vendor's own MCP server, from our MCP research; it works with your own account at the vendor.
